conviction_note: Two sourced forces pull in opposite directions and roughly offset. (1) The single-source EPS bar ($1.21, -23% YoY) looks low against the run-rate: Q4 FY25's $1.58 was flattered by a 4.8% tax rate, and Q3 FY26 adjusted operating income fell only 9.9% on +250bp of gross margin. (2) Diesel ran from ~$4.96 in July to a record $6.53 on Sept 21, after management said on Aug 5 that it had moderated, so the Q4 freight hit should exceed Q3's ~$5M. impact_sum is +0.4 and the scaled number +0.28 (p_up 52 on a 7.0 abs move). The beat is the likelier print (print_vs_bar +8%), but last year a 33% EPS beat bought only +1.1%, the stock is +8.6% over 20 days, and the first FY27 commentary will be set against record fuel, so the reaction is held near a coin flip.
bar: Adjusted EPS $1.21 on revenue $400.5M (year ago $1.58 / $410.2M), Earnings Whispers preview dated 2026-11-10 (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/JJSF/23125, mirrored at https://finviz.com/news/420699/jj-snack-foods-must-show-apollo-savings-can-outrun-freight-as-fy27-growth-pledge-nears). A separate Earnings Whispers stock page shows $1.32 EPS on the same $400.5M revenue (https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/JJSF), so the EPS bar is disputed. Coverage is 3-4 analysts. The company gives no numeric guidance. Every EPS-dependent finding is capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest is 962.5K shares at the 2026-10-30 settlement, up 8.65% from 885.9K. Days to cover is 5.03 against a 24-report average of 3.62 (https://www.optionsanalysissuite.com/stocks/jjsf/short-interest). That is about 5.1% of the 18.75M shares outstanding (10-Q, May 2026) and roughly 6% of float, since the founder's trust holds 18.7%. Shorts are rising and above their own average but not crowded. There is no usable option chain (ATM spread 140% of mid, open interest 111, no skew), so the market makes no directional statement through options. The tape: +8.59% over 20 days, -0.64% over 5 days, 9.7% below the 52-week high. The stock is up ~10.7% since the Aug 5 print, per the Nov 10 preview.

findings.finding: The $1.21 EPS bar (-23% YoY) sits below a run-rate built from the company's own numbers. Q4 FY25 adjusted EPS of $1.58 included a 4.8% effective tax rate (normalised, its $37.7M adjusted operating income is about $1.45). In Q3 FY26 adjusted operating income fell only 9.9% and gross margin rose ~250bp to 35.5% on Apollo plant savings. Applying Q3's -10% to Q4's $37.7M gives ~$34M, about $1.35 on ~18.7M shares at a 25% tax rate, roughly 10% above $1.21. The company has beaten this thin bar big twice in a row: Q4 FY25 $1.58 vs $1.19, Q3 FY26 $1.96 vs $1.70.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The EPS beats were paid unevenly. Q4 FY25's +33% EPS beat with a revenue miss moved +1.13% (2025-11-17, baseline). Q3 FY26's ~15% EPS beat on margins moved +7.66% (2026-08-05, baseline; consensus per https://247wallst.com/cards/j-j-snack-foods-q3-2026-earnings-jjsf-01kz8sy3z1ydaxc1jd66twxm72). Q1 and Q2 FY26 fell -15.4% and -7.0% on sales declines.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market expected ~$1.35, the published consensus would not imply -23% YoY. The preview frames Q4 as 'earnings expected to fall by nearly a quarter'. The tax-rate distortion in the year-ago $1.58 is in the FY25 8-K body (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/785956/000143774925035287/ex_889324.htm, 2025-11-17), not in the headline comparison. Partly priced: the stock is +8.6% over 20 days, and the bar itself is disputed ($1.32 on another Earnings Whispers page).
findings.independence: Same-company documents only: the Q3 FY26 8-K and the Q4 FY25 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/785956/000143774925035287/ex_889324.htm). Beat history from 247wallst (Q3) and a secondary summary of Q4 FY25 (https://www-web.itiger.com/news/1158171896). This is an inference, not a disclosed Q4 number. The diesel finding below works against it.

findings.finding: Diesel, JJSF's biggest swing cost in distribution, rose through the fiscal fourth quarter (~Jun 28 to Sep 26, 2026). The monthly average was $4.96 in July (+31% YoY), ~$5.45 by mid-August, and a record $6.53 in the week of Sep 21, up ~$2.78/gal YoY. On Aug 5 management had blamed ~$4.7-5.0M of net fuel and freight cost for distribution reaching 11.6% of sales and said diesel had moderated from summer highs. The Q4 hit should therefore exceed Q3's, and the first FY27 commentary will be given with diesel still above $6 (week of Oct 5).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Freight and fuel was the headline drag in Q3 FY26 and the stock still rose +7.66%, because gross margin outran it. In the FY26 quarters where sales and costs both disappointed, the stock fell -15.4% (Feb) and -7.0% (May).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The Nov 10 preview says management warned freight pressure would continue, and the -23% EPS consensus may already embed it. What is not visible: management's last word (Aug 5) was that diesel had moderated, and the Sept spike to a 32-year record came after it. Since then the stock has risen 10.7% and sentiment has 'softened considerably' from bearish, which is not what a market braced for a bigger freight hit looks like.
findings.independence: Separate diesel sources agree: July avg $4.96 (https://www.supplychain247.com/article/diesel-prices-july-2026-year-over-year-trucking-fuel-costs/40150), week of Sep 7 $5.97 (+$2.20 YoY) (https://casterhq.com/blogs/industrial-insights/eia-puts-us-on-highway-diesel-at-5-967-for-the-week-of-sept-7-2026), EIA (https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=68164). The company has not confirmed the Q4 figure, so macro-to-company transmission is a proxy. Fuel surcharges and higher minimum orders partly offset it.

findings.finding: Theater attendance, an outlet for the ICEE frozen-beverage segment (~25% of sales), was strong in JJSF's fiscal Q4. AMC's US attendance was 52.13M in Jul-Sep 2026, +23.3% YoY, and US food & beverage per patron rose to $8.85 from $8.55. The year-ago Frozen Beverages segment fell 8.3% to $99.6M lapping Inside Out 2, an easy comparison. In Q3 FY26 beverage sales had already risen $4.2M while machine and service sales fell $10.7M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Frozen Beverages drove a revenue miss in Q4 FY25 (-8.3% segment), when the stock moved only +1.13%. There is no clean history of this segment alone moving the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: Revenue consensus is $400.5M, -2.4% YoY, against a segment comparison that was down 8.3% last year and a quarter in which the domestic box office reportedly topped $3B. If the theater lift were priced, the revenue bar would sit nearer flat. Net of the rest: theaters are only part of ICEE, which is also sold through c-stores (weak, see the next finding) and machine sales (falling). Food Service (~60% of sales) still carries ~$16M a quarter of planned bakery SKU exits.
findings.independence: AMC's results coverage (https://www.stocktitan.net/articles/amc-q3-2026-earnings-record-revenue-net-profit) and domestic Q3 box office reports (https://digg.com/entertainment/0frjv9wq). Both are proxies; JJSF has not confirmed. The c-store finding below partly offsets it.

findings.finding: Convenience-store and gas-station traffic, ICEE's other main outlet, was weak into the quarter. Placer.ai showed gas-station visits down 4.1% YoY in the week of June 29, 2026, on high pump prices. PepsiCo's CEO named gas stations and c-stores as impulse channels where traffic was converting less. JJSF had already said frozen-beverage sales in c-stores lagged.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No isolated history; c-store softness was part of the Q3 FY26 frozen-beverage decline (-5.8%), on a day the stock rose +7.66%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the company itself flagged c-store weakness and the Nov 10 preview repeats it. Filed small because diesel kept rising through September, which by this mechanism prolongs the traffic drag beyond the quarter management last described.
findings.independence: Shares its mechanism (high fuel prices) with the diesel finding but lands on a different line (ICEE demand, not distribution cost). A proxy; no company-level number.

findings.finding: JJSF raised its dividend in November 2025, to $0.80 from $0.78. The rate was held at $0.80 in August 2026, so a November raise, after five consecutive years of increases, may come with the Q4 release. The buyback authorization has only $18M left of $50M after $74.7M was repurchased in FY26 YTD, so a new authorization is plausible; that spending was partly funded by $28M of new debt and cash falling to $63.1M from $105.9M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The November 2025 raise coincided with the +1.13% Q4 FY25 reaction; it cannot be separated.
findings.why_not_priced: A raise is customary and largely expected. A new buyback authorization would be incremental, but it is not confirmed. A held dividend would be read as a negative.
findings.independence: Q3 FY26 8-K for the buyback remainder and balance sheet (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000785956/000143774926025782/ex_998849.htm).

findings.finding: Short interest is building into the print: 962.5K shares at the Oct 30 settlement, +8.65% period on period, with 5.03 days to cover against a 24-report average of 3.62 (~5% of shares outstanding). On a beat, short covering adds to the upside on a ~197K-share-a-day name.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is a mechanism rather than information. At ~5% of shares it is moderate, not the 18-23% float shorts that squeezed in the lessons file.
findings.independence: An aggregator snippet showed ~6.0% of float and 6.5 days to cover at the early-October settlement (https://equibles.com/stocks/jjsf/summary, snippet only).

outside_window.finding: The founder Gerald Shreiber died on 2026-05-14. The largest holder is the 2021 Irrevocable Trust for Gerald B. Shreiber, with ~3.5M shares (18.7%). Any estate sale, distribution or strategic consequence has no date and is not expected inside the window. A lead independent director was appointed on 2026-08-24.

baseline_tension: There is no option skew to agree or disagree with. The +8.6% 20-day run-up and 'softened' sentiment mean some of the beat case is already in the price, while the September diesel spike cuts against it, so the evidence leaves p_up near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (bar unsourced or disputed: $1.21 vs $1.32, one source family): EPS-beat finding capped from +1.5 to +1.0; print_vs_bar cut from +12 to +8.
Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the Q4 FY25 33% beat bought only +1.1%, which kept the beat finding small and p_up at 52 rather than higher.
Lesson 5 (proxies smaller): diesel -2.0 to -1.5, theater attendance +1.0 to +0.7, c-store traffic -0.5 to -0.3, all filed with independence marked as proxy.
Lesson 7 (look up short interest before a negative): ~5% short with 5 days to cover is not crowded, so the diesel negative was not shrunk further; positioning finding cut +0.3 to +0.2.
Lesson 8 (thin coverage): abs_move held at the 7.0 median rather than shrunk, because this print carries the first FY27 commentary.
